cards.title: Where SQL came from
cards.text: Edgar F. Codd described the relational model at IBM in 1970. IBM researchers then built SEQUEL, later renamed SQL, to query it.

cards.title: ACID
cards.text: Transactions in relational databases aim to be ACID: Atomic (all or nothing), Consistent (rules hold), Isolated (no interference from concurrent transactions) and Durable (committed data survives crashes).

cards.title: Indexes aren't free
cards.text: An index speeds up reads, but every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE must also update the index, so writes get slower and storage grows.

cards.question: Which SQL clause filters groups after aggregation?
cards.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters the groups afterwards.

What does a primary key guarantee?
cards.answer: Every row has a unique, non-null key

cards.statement: In SQL, NULL = NULL evaluates to true.
cards.explanation: Comparing with NULL gives NULL (unknown). Use IS NULL to test for it.

cards.statement: Adding an index to a table can make INSERTs slower.
cards.explanation: Each insert must also add an entry to every index on the table.

code: CREATE TABLE s (dept TEXT, pay INT);
GROUP BY dept ORDER BY dept;
cards.explanation: GROUP BY collapses the rows for each dept into one, and SUM adds their pay.

code: LEFT JOIN b ON a.id = b.id;
cards.explanation: Rows 1 and 3 have no match and appear once each; row 2 matches twice, giving 1 + 2 + 1 = 4.

cards.explanation: A B-tree is balanced, so a lookup walks one path from root to leaf.
